transcript: Potentially hot take around the Hamilton Screenings controversy. But I kind of understand why people are complaining because we don't know. Hamilton is being shown in movie theaters for the very first time, and at the top of that screening, they play a message from Lin Manuel Miranda encouraging the audience to sing along. And so people have been taking that as permission to sing along. But with that, you also had another group of audience members complaining because this was not advertised as a sing along performance, and they just wanted to watch the movie without people singing around them. And I definitely think this is a case where both sides are kind of right. People singing along are right to do so because they were given permission to. But I also understand that sing along performances are not something that everyone enjoys. And the fact that this was not advertised as a sing along screening, it was probably pretty jarring for these people. Do I think that anyone should be yelling at the people around them to stop singing? Absolutely not. But I do understand the people that went to the movie theater and said, hey, this is not what I paid for and asked for a refund. Because I don't think that these people would have bought tickets if they knew it was a sing along screening. And I do wish that they had made this clear from the start or made specific screenings sing along screenings. And specific screenings, non sing along screenings. Because as it stands now, if you're excited to see Hamilton on the big screen, but you don't want to attend a sing along screening, you're kind of out of luck.
